subject: Re: Long-context evals — model recommendations & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Long-context evals — follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the discovery call today — great context on the document-heavy workflows you
run for Acme Legal & Research. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Main pain: models truncating critical legal context at ~8k–32k tokens, causing missing clauses in summaries and hallucinated redactions.
- Important metrics for you: recall of key clauses, summarization fidelity (legalese->plain language), and deterministic handling of long documents.
- Security: on-prem / VPC requirement for PII-heavy files.

Our initial recommendations (based on the samples you shared):
- Candidate models to evaluate: redwood-llm-xlarge-v2 (64k context variant) for best fidelity/latency balance; llama-3-70b-instruct-quant (8-bit) as a cost-optimized baseline.
- For very long archives (100k+ tokens), we recommend Redwood’s long-context pipeline: chunked prefix encoding + KV cache with our 128k context runtime (experimental) — this minimizes truncation for retrieval-style prompts.
- Prompting & evaluation: we’ll run the following prompt sets (attached): "legal_summarization_prompts.csv" and "clause_recall_prompts.csv".

Deliverables / next steps:
1) We’ll produce a short POC bundle (benchmarks + sample outputs) within 7 business days: baseline quality numbers, token costs, and truncation breakdowns. (Attachment: acme-long-context-eval-benchmarks.pdf)
2) Marcus will scope the dedicated runtime config and security checklist (VPC, KMS) and propose an environment for a 2-week POC.
3) Schedule a 30-min POC kickoff to align on datasets + success criteria.

Questions I have for you to prep the POC:
- Which success metric do you want prioritized (recall vs. compression/concise summary)?
- Are we allowed to use a redacted set of real documents or prefer synthetic holdouts?

I’ve attached the prompt sets and a short benchmark plan. Happy to hop on a quick call this week to finalize scope.

Best,

Subject: Long-context evals — truncation, caching, and POC plan

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the sample set (received). Below are answers to your specific questions and a refined POC plan.

Truncation behavior (64k variant):
- The redwood-llm-xlarge-v2 64k context mode maintains a sliding KV cache and does not naively drop tokens from the left. For document->summary flows we recommend: 
  1) Prefix the prompt with a 1–2 sentence instruction + the document chunking index.
  2) Use our chunked recall API that inserts retrieved passages with metadata; this avoids losing remote clauses.
- Caveat: single-token-attention architectures still have practical limits on positional encodings. For documents >64k we do either: (a) hierarchical summarization (chunk -> summarize -> synthesize) or (b) the experimental 128k runtime (available for POCs) which uses a hybrid chunk+KV strategy. We will include both pipelines in the benchmark.

Summarization fidelity & benchmarks:
- See attached PDF for side-by-side examples: we include a "gold" legal summary, model outputs, and an automated recall score for clause-level retrieval. Preliminary results show the 64k variant preserves >92% of key clauses on our legal test suite vs ~78% for standard 32k runs (numbers will be in the POC report).

POC plan / timeline:
- Day 0–2: confirm dataset (redacted sample) and success criteria (recall threshold, average token cost).
- Day 3–7: run benchmarks (64k variant, 8-bit cost baseline, hierarchical pipeline). Deliverable: PDF + example outputs + cost spreadsheet.
- Week 2: two-week in-environment trial for integration tests (if you want dedicated capacity or VPC we’ll scope infra in parallel).

Security / compliance note:
- For PII-heavy docs we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) and encrypted KMS keys. Marcus will queue the security checklist and an SOC2 artifact pack if Priya needs it.

Next execs / asks:
- Marcus will propose the POC infra and join the kickoff to scope logs/retention.
- Can you confirm whether redacted samples are okay or if we need a formal DPA amendment?

I’ve re-attached the prompt sets and the partial benchmark export.

Best,

Marissa Cole
